chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: that he was asked about a man—whether it is proper for him to perform salat while a woman is performing salat in front of him. He said:

He should not perform salat until he places between himself and her more than ten cubits. And if she is on his right or on his left, he should place between himself and her the like of that. But if she is performing salat behind him, then there is no problem, even if she reaches his garment. And if the woman is sitting, sleeping, or standing without being in salat, then there is no problem wherever she may be.

key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits as a required distance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man performing salat when a woman is praying in front of or beside him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the relative positioning of a man and a woman during salat when both are praying. It distinguishes between a woman praying in front of, beside, or behind the man, and also clarifies that her mere presence outside of salat does not cause a problem.
